correctness.rationale: The theorem gives a complete exactly quantified classification of \(C_k(N)\) for all \(N\ge2\) with at most two distinct prime factors and all \(k\ge0\). Radical scaling follows from gcd equivalence. The CRT reduces counts to local fibers. For primes 2,3,5 the first-six fibers are explicitly tabulated; for all primes >=7 a fiber contains at most two of six indices and the first-three squares are distinct. Checking assignments for index lengths 1..5 yields the displayed counts, and a direct examination of each unique length-five survivor rules out index six. Monotonicity rules out every later length. A standalone script independently matched gcd counts over 1,059 eligible moduli \(\le1600\) and CRT counts over 210 prime pairs; finite tests are supporting evidence rather than proof.

value.rationale: The named polynomial-Jacobsthal invariant naturally asks how many local prime obstructions suffice to cover initial polynomial values. The first nontrivial support size is exactly two primes: their root fibers interact. The theorem supplies an infinite complete spectrum for all exponents and all prime pairs, including sharp exceptional behavior at primes 2,3,5, and exact frequency/unique-extremal-class information absent from a maximum-only classification. It is a concrete structural benchmark for the local covering mechanism and is not merely a finite search or a numerical tiny improvement.
